title: ROM
body:
**Read-Only Memory**: non-volatile storage whose contents survive a power cycle. It holds
the code that has to exist before anything else does, the boot firmware, which on the
Atari ST is the TOS ROM.

The reason it sits in the [[Combinational Logic]] section is that a ROM *is* a
combinational circuit. Address in, data out, no state, no clock. An $n$-bit address with
$m$-bit words is a lookup table of $2^n$ rows, which means any truth table with $n$ inputs
and $m$ outputs can be implemented by burning it into a ROM instead of minimising it into
gates. Slower and larger than dedicated logic, but you can change it without rewiring, and
it is how microcode-driven control units work.

Under [[Memory Mapping]], ROM occupies part of the same address space as RAM and the
[[I-O Interface]] registers; a [[Decoder]] on the high address bits decides which one the
[[CPU]] is actually talking to.
